newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says elections, donor summit key for Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy says elections, donor summit key for Albania.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday that Italy considered it vital for Albania's planned general election to go ahead by the end of June.
"Rapid and transparent elections to allow the immediate removal of troops and to confirm that the crisis is temporary are essential," Prodi told a conference on Albania.

He said Italy's second goal was to organise a "conference of donors" attended by the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund, European experts and Albanian authorities to discuss economic aid for Albania. No date has yet been set.
"If Europe gets involved, it is possible to do (this). There are funds available," Prodi said.
He also called for the creation of an international coordination group to work with Albanian authorities to rebuild the judicial, banking and school systems, but did not elaborate.

Albanian political parties told international mediator Franz Vranitzky last week that they wanted to hold the election on June 29. Foreign Minister Arjan Starova told reporters in Vienna on Monday that the vote would go ahead in June as planned.

Italy is leading a multinational U.N.-backed force, dubbed Operation Alba, to secure humanitarian aid to Europe's poorest country following an armed insurrection sparked by the collapse of dubious savings schemes earlier this year.
The force has an initial three month mandate and Italy has said it hopes the troops can withdraw one month after elections.
